Question: Triangle \(ABC\) has side-lengths \(AB = 12,\) \(BC = 24,\) and \(AC = 18.\) The line through the incenter of \(\triangle ABC\) parallel to \(\overline{BC}\) intersects \(\overline{AB}\) at \(M\) and \(\overline{AC}\) at \(N.\) What is the perimeter of \(\triangle AMN?\)
Solution:
Method 1: Cancel equal segments

Let \(I\) be the incenter. The angle bisectors and the parallel line create equal segments that can replace the unknown pieces of the perimeter. Since \(I\) is inside the triangle, it lies between \(M\) and \(N\).

Because \(BI\) bisects angle \(ABC\) and \(IM\parallel BC\),
\[
\angle MBI=\angle IBC=\angle BIM.
\]
Thus triangle \(BMI\) has two equal angles, so \(BM=MI\). Likewise, the angle bisector \(CI\) and \(IN\parallel BC\) give
\[
\angle NCI=\angle BCI=\angle CIN,
\]
so \(CN=NI\).

Now write the smaller triangle's perimeter using the original sides:
\[
\begin{aligned}
AM+AN+MN
&=(AB-BM)+(AC-CN)+(MI+IN)\\
&=AB+AC\\
&=12+18=\boxed{30}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

Method 2: Compare the inradius and altitude

The line through the incenter is parallel to the base, so its distance above the base determines the scale of the smaller triangle. Let \(r>0\) be the inradius, \(h>0\) the altitude from \(A\) to line \(BC\), and \(K\) the area of triangle \(ABC\).

The incenter has perpendicular distance \(r\) from each side. Joining it to the three vertices partitions the triangle into three triangles, giving
\[
K=\frac12r(12+24+18)=27r.
\]
Using \(BC\) as the base also gives \(K=\frac12\cdot24h=12h\). Therefore
\[
\frac rh=\frac{12}{27}=\frac49.
\]
Since \(MN\) passes through the incenter and is parallel to \(BC\), it is \(r\) above \(BC\). Triangle \(AMN\) consequently has altitude \(h-r\). The two triangles are similar by their equal corresponding angles, with length scale
\[
\frac{h-r}{h}=1-\frac49=\frac59.
\]
Their perimeters have this same ratio, so the requested perimeter is
\[
\frac59(12+24+18)=\boxed{30},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
